We are getting to the point that our language is actually dying.

Marvel called these two a "post-ironic meditation".

Post. Ironic.

Our categories are losing their meaning. I know there are people who hear this phrase, however, and think, "Wow, that sounds really cool, progressive, and intellectual." In reality, it's just a completely senseless term that let's people hide other nonsense behind it because it has a vague fog of culture critique surrounding it, so it's obviously something.

I gave up trying to keep track of such categories years ago. They are meaningless. We are not divided into discrete categories, we are a continuous process. There are no "generations." There are only people. When does the "baby boomer" generation end? When did "gen X" start? Sure, we can set arbitrary dates, but that's what they are -- abritrary. These labels are just shorthand for those who find thinking exhausting. Modern. Post-modern. Post-post-modern. Just noise.

I agree insofar as we're saying that humans being a "continuous process" implies that consciousness is a continual interpretation. Categories are not real except to the extent they participate as part of the interpretative experience and obtain an implicit use, so long as we find that our experience has purpose - creates pleasure, dissolves displeasure, inheres us with significance. I think this is true of all language. There is no truth with a capital T, only agreements and sympathies with interpretive frames (that can be effectively communicated). I think we get into trouble, however, when we try to argue for dismissing the importance of our labels altogether. They are real. They are artifacts of a form of experience, and they persist to the extent that others either sympathize with that experience (as they understand it to have occurred), or that they can be convinced to adopt that frame of interpretation, thereby granting human realness to the terms that were used. We all succumb to digitizing our continuous reality into discrete concepts. It's the only way we can confer meaning to anything at all.

It's really an issue of power and will when it comes to the "success" of any given label. This is why they are important. They form the scaffolding of a particular frame of interpreting reality (and thereby cause us to experience that reality in a certain way). So labels become an expression of a fundamental sort of power. Our rejection or support of these labels reflects how we are interpreting reality.

For that reason, I don't believe we can say that labels are perfectly arbitrary. They have degrees of arbitrariness. But since all of our interpretations are caused, to some degree, by our own past experience and the past interpretations of our culture and social circles, they aren't perfectly arbitrary. They contain history. In my own opinion, the terms classic or pre-modern, modern, and post-modern are useful concepts. I don't reject them. The term post-ironic is senseless to me. When we use terms gauging the modernity of something, we are working inside of historical boundaries, making value judgments. The term "ironic" is a universal quality that doesn't lose what it is attempting to convey based on what we are referring to, it doesn't matter at all whether we are referring to 10,000 years ago, or a fictional event in the future. Post-ironic is nonsense because it implies there was a historical point where irony ceased to exist.
